problem:
What is the linear transformation $T$ whose standard matrix is 
$T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}]?$

examples.worked_solution:
Consider a general vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14048912/assets/c5e95c3c6c86e0719be77fc3db865c7a81995ef386ce7508ccef19ab307a783a.png) Multiplying by the matrix $T,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -1 \\ -5 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8x-y \\ -5x-2y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the linear transformation $\,\mathbf{T}\,$ is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14048912/assets/e6c0ddd895406c6b79e4c520a7a4002060c917b51a6070f134be8c47dd63de0b.png)

feedback.problem:
Find the standard matrix that  represents  the  linear  transformation $T$, where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x \\ x-y\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 2$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2\cdot x+0\cdot y \\ 1\cdot x+(-1)\cdot y\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2x \\ x-y\end{aligned}].
$$

    Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$
